Container.Name: mangapixer
Container.Overview: MangaPixer is a self-hosted comic and manga server with a fast web reader for desktop, tablet and phone. It is folder-native: point it at your existing folders of .cbz and .cbr archives and it shows them exactly as they are organized on disk - no renaming, no metadata to curate, and your media is only ever read. Features per-user reading progress and read marks, continue reading and new-chapter rows, single, double-page and vertical (webtoon) reading with right-to-left support, favorites, search, private libraries, and server-side image resizing that keeps line art and screentones clean on every screen. Optional series information - descriptions, authors, covers, volumes and which volumes or chapters you are missing - comes from ComicInfo.xml inside your archives and, only if an admin turns it on, from MangaUpdates, MangaDex, AniList, the Grand Comics Database (comics and graphic novels) and Wikipedia (volume lists). An admin can also create API tokens so another app on your network (such as MangaList) can read that series information and, if allowed, ask for a library scan after it adds files. Accounts are created by an admin; there are no default credentials and no telemetry, and nothing leaves your server until an admin turns on an optional internet feature (the update check or series information).
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: manga comics comic reader webtoon manhwa cbz cbr yacreader
Container.Requires: Your comics or manga as .cbz / .zip or non-solid .cbr / .rar archives in a share. Solid archives (including every .cb7 / .7z) are listed but cannot be read yet.
Container.Changes: ### 2026-10-07 - Overview: an API token can also be allowed to ask for a library scan (MangaPixer 1.36.0); nothing new leaves your server. ### 2026-10-03 - Overview: read-only API tokens let another app on your network (such as MangaList) read the series information (MangaPixer 1.33.0); nothing new leaves your server on its own. ### 2026-10-02 - Overview: comics and graphic novels from the Grand Comics Database and volume lists from Wikipedia (MangaPixer 1.32.0; off until an admin turns them on), part of what may leave your server. ### 2026-10-01 - Overview: optional series information from MangaUpdates, MangaDex and AniList (off until an admin turns it on), and what leaves your server. ### 2026-09-23 - Listed in Community Applications. Release notes: https://github.com/dixit92/mangapixer/releases

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the web UI. The server listens on 8080 inside the container.

Config.Name: Appdata
Config.Description: Where MangaPixer keeps its database, backups, thumbnails and page cache. Back this folder up.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: A share with your comics or manga, mounted read-only (for example /mnt/user/Manga). For more shares, use Add another Path with a sibling container path such as /media/comics, read-only - never mount one share inside another. In the web app, register each one as a library (for example /media/manga).

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID that owns the appdata folder (99 = nobody on most Unraid systems; check with ls -ln /mnt/user/appdata).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID that owns the appdata folder (100 = users on most Unraid systems).

Config.Name: Data Root
Config.Description: Database, sign-in keys, logs, backups and thumbnails, inside the appdata folder. Leave as is.

Config.Name: Cache Root
Config.Description: Page image cache (disposable), inside the appdata folder. Leave as is.

Config.Name: Scratch Root
Config.Description: Temporary work files (disposable), inside the appdata folder. Leave as is.
